title: Unsigned uncurrying and derived comparison on integral Hom representatives
statement: Let Y be a scheme and R a commutative ring sheaf on its pro-etale site, with the indicated sheafification and local-bijection criteria. Use the module complexes, K-flat predicate, and Hom-model map of [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models], and a closed coefficient structure S and tensor models T of [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. For K-flat complexes P,L, any complex I, and any chain map phi:P -> Hom(L,I), there is a chain map a:Tot(P tensor L) -> I. On the summand of degrees p,q with p+q=k it sends x tensor y to the p,q,k Hom-product projection of phi(x), evaluated at y, with no sign. Under the fixed tensor comparison, Q(a) is the inverse transpose of Q(phi) followed by the fixed Hom-model map. The product projections are those of [lem-sc-hom-complex-projections].

source.place: paragraph 2, coefficient extension; representative evaluation normalization

proof.text: Uncurry phi using the existing chain equivalence between total-tensor maps and Hom-complex maps. Its component formula is unsigned evaluation in the order P tensor L.

Postcompose phi with the fixed injective-resolution augmentation and apply T.uncurry_model. Equality on every pure tensor in every total summand identifies the chain map supplied there with chain uncurrying of the augmented phi. This extensionality follows by total-coproduct extensionality, module sheafification adjunction, and ordinary tensor generation.

Naturality of chain uncurrying identifies the augmented uncurry with the original uncurry followed by the augmentation. Localize and compose with the inverse localized augmentation; its product is the identity. The definition of homModelMap then gives the stated derived comparison.
